==Problem==

The letters <math>A</math>, <math>B</math>, <math>C</math> and <math>D</math> represent digits. If  <math> \begin{tabular}{ccc}&A&B\\ +&C&A\\ \hline &D&A\end{tabular} </math>and <math> \begin{tabular}{ccc}&A&B\\ -&C&A\\ \hline &&A\end{tabular} </math>,what digit does <math>D</math> represent?

<math> \textbf{(A)}\ 5\qquad\textbf{(B)}\ 6\qquad\textbf{(C)}\ 7\qquad\textbf{(D)}\ 8\qquad\textbf{(E)}\ 9 </math>

==Solution==

Because <imath> B+A=A </imath>, <imath>B</imath> must be <imath>0</imath>.
Next, because <imath> B-A=A\implies0-A=A,</imath> we get <imath>A=5</imath> as the "0" mentioned above is actually 10 in this case. 

Now we can rewrite <imath> \begin{tabular}{ccc}&A&0\\ +&C&A\\ \hline &D&A\end{tabular} </imath> as <imath> \begin{tabular}{ccc}&5&0\\ +&C&5\\ \hline &D&5\end{tabular} </imath>. Therefore, <imath>D=5+C.</imath>

Finally, <imath> A-1-C=0\implies{A=C+1}\implies{C=4} </imath>, So we have <imath> D=5+C\implies{D=5+4}=\boxed{\textbf{(E)}\ 9 } </imath>.
